method.move: DEMove 0.8 and DESnookerMove 0.2 (ter Braak 2006, https://doi.org/10.1007/s11222-006-8769-1; ter Braak and Vrugt 2008, https://doi.org/10.1007/s11222-008-9104-9)
method.likelihood: Gaussian on the measured throughput [t/h] and power [kW]: engine(theta) + discrepancy + noise, the discrepancy (a constant and slopes on standardized CSS and f80, N(0, tau^2) each) integrated out exactly
method.p80: not a target: it is not measured
method.interval_80: the 10th and 90th percentiles of the posterior predictive draws of the held-out survey

priors.name: q_ref_tph
priors.source: nominal: Rocha et al. 2024, https://doi.org/10.3390/min14090919, Table 4 (QT about 647 t/h); width: weakly informative, a log standard deviation of 0.25 (plus or minus 28 percent); the surveys span 813 to 1639 t/h

priors.name: wi_kwh_t
priors.source: nominal: the blend Wi of the engine; the compact and supercompact itabirite bands are 7.2 and 10.6 kWh/t (Rocha et al. 2024, https://doi.org/10.3390/min14090919, Table 1, as HP500_ORE); width: weakly informative, a log standard deviation of 0.17 (plus or minus 18 percent, 7.6 to 10.7 kWh/t)

priors.name: zeta
priors.source: nominal: the slope of Pc = zeta Pd + Pn, Rocha et al. 2024, https://doi.org/10.3390/min14090919, Table 5; width: weakly informative, a log standard deviation of 0.23 (plus or minus 26 percent)

priors.name: pn_kw
priors.source: nominal: the no-load power of Pc = zeta Pd + Pn, Rocha et al. 2024, https://doi.org/10.3390/min14090919, Table 5; width: weakly informative, standard deviation 50 kW; the measured power spans 187 to 355 kW

priors.name: k1_scale
priors.source: multiplier of K1 = 0.23 CSS + 0.30 f80 (Rocha et al. 2024, https://doi.org/10.3390/min14090919, Table 5); width: a log standard deviation of 0.15 (plus or minus 16 percent)

priors.name: k2_scale
priors.source: multiplier of K2 = 12.0 + 0.55 CSS + 0.40 f80 (Rocha et al. 2024, https://doi.org/10.3390/min14090919, Table 5); width: a log standard deviation of 0.15

priors.name: k3
priors.source: nominal: Rocha et al. 2024, https://doi.org/10.3390/min14090919, Table 5; the typical K3 of the cone models of the engine runs 2.0 to 2.7 (Napier-Munn et al. 1996, Mineral Comminution Circuits, JKMRC); width: standard deviation 0.5

priors.name: t10_shift_pct
priors.source: shift of the constant 64 of t10 (%) = 64 - 0.12 CSS - 0.23 f80 (Rocha et al. 2024, https://doi.org/10.3390/min14090919, Table 5); width: standard deviation 4 points of t10 (the engine caps t10 at 44 percent)

convergence.criterion: converged when the post-burn chain is at least 50 integrated autocorrelation times long (emcee get_autocorr_time, largest over the parameters); a failing posterior is recorded as not converged

comparators_note: scored on the same ten surveys: B_lin, M0 (the CrusherCal band) and M2 with the nested 80 percent band of loo.nested_band_coverage (sigma of each survey from the other nine held-out residuals)
contraction_note: posterior over prior standard deviation on the fit to all ten surveys; below 0.5 the surveys identify the parameter, near 1 it stays at its prior; the discrepancy rows are the exact conditional of the coefficients given the engine scalars

kill_criterion.rule: dropped as a predictor if (a) power LOO MAPE is not below B-lin's by at least 3 points and the throughput LOO MAPE does not beat the backbone M0's by at least 3 points, and (b) on either target the coverage lies outside 0.7 to 0.9 or the mean band is wider than the CrusherCal band
